data.claim: recover labels a DONE item [expired_lease] because complete keeps the lapsed lease and release is a no-op on it; skipping terminal items in the expired-lease scan makes it read done
data.probe: regression test asserting no expired_lease finding for a completed item with a lapsed lease
data.question: Why does recover label a DONE item expired_lease, and what should it read instead?

evidence.note: CONFIRMED R9e1feaaaca: recovery.scan reported ANY not-live lease as expired_lease before checking it.terminal, so a DONE item whose lease complete never clears read as a crash orphan; skipping terminal items (via _expired_lease helper) reads it done.

commit fe29d7309: ddflow/services/leases/recovery.py _expired_lease helper skips terminal items; tests/test_recover_merged_item.py regression test_a_done_item_with_a_lapsed_lease_reads_done_not_expired_lease

chunk_findings.detail: The new predicate suppresses the `expired_lease` finding for every terminal item, not only for terminal items that are actually clean-and-fully-merged as the bug motivates. Given an item that is terminal (e.g. completed or cancelled) but whose lapsed lease still has/points to a worktree containing unmerged changes, `_expired_lease` returns `False` solely because `it.terminal` is true, so `scan` skips the entire expired-lease branch. That branch contains the logic that prefers whichever source names a tree and surfaces real salvageable work; before this change, the same input would enter the branch and report an expired-lease/salvage finding. The result is a false negative for real unmerged work, while the stated fix was only meant to stop clean merged done items from being labelled `[expired_lease]`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/recovery.py:_expired_lease

chunk_findings.detail: Given a `DONE` item whose lease has lapsed and whose worktree is not clean-and-fully-merged (for example, an unmerged commit is made in that worktree after `item.completed`, or completion was recorded while the tree was still dirty), `_expired_lease` returns `False` solely because `it.state == DONE`. `scan` therefore skips the expired-lease branch that previously surfaced the lapsed lease and the worktree, so `ddflow recover` can hide salvageable work. The stated intent is to suppress the stale `[expired_lease]` label only for clean-and-fully-merged `DONE` items, but the predicate checks only state and does not verify that the worktree is clean and fully merged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/recovery.py:_expired_lease

data.probe: A DONE item cannot hide salvageable work: complete records item.completed only after merge landed its sha on the base (_landed_on_base requires merge gate passed AND the sha reachable from base), so a DONE items own commits are always on base; any residual post-completion commit in a kept worktree is scratch, not lost work. The predicate keys on state==DONE, not terminal, so an ABANDONED item (also terminal) is NOT skipped. This is the same invariant _note_landed already states: a finished item is owed nothing.

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper suppresses the `expired_lease` finding for every item whose `state` is `DONE`, but the bug only justifies suppressing the label when the item is actually clean-and-fully-merged. `scan` already has access to worktree/Git facts, and `DONE` by itself is not a proof that the branch/worktree is clean and fully merged at scan time (for example, a DONE item can still have an absent `merged_sha`, unmerged commits, or a dirty worktree after completion). For such an input, `_expired_lease` returns `False` solely because of the state check, so `scan` emits no `expired_lease` recovery and `ddflow recover`/`lanes` stop surfacing a crash-orphan that may still contain salvageable work. This is a false negative; the condition should test the clean-and-fully-merged state (or otherwise clear the stale lease) rather than treating `DONE` as sufficient.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/recovery.py:_expired_lease

data.probe: completion ENFORCES the invariant the finding assumes away: finish.py:198 `hard += CM._own_branch_unmerged(...)` makes an unmerged own branch a HARD blocker that is never force-liftable (finish.py:62 "an unmerged own branch is never force-liftable"), so a DONE item cannot hold unmerged commits by construction; its own commits are on base. A dirty KEPT worktree on a DONE item is post-ship scratch, not unshipped work. state==DONE keys also on the exact surface the bug names, and ABANDONED (terminal but NOT done) is NOT skipped, so real salvageable work stays reportable.
